previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of recurrent lower extremity erythema due to lipodermatosclerosis and chronic venous insufficiency was admitted for bilateral leg redness and swelling that recurred after starting suppressive minocycline. She was afebrile without leukocytosis or other signs of infection. IV antibiotics were initially started but discontinued after infectious disease and dermatology evaluation confirmed an inflammatory rather than infectious etiology. She was treated with a seven-day course of topical clobetasol with plastic wrap and miconazole cream for the toes. Her chronic conditions, including diastolic heart failure, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and chronic pancreatitis, remained stable on home medications. She improved clinically and was discharged home with dermatology follow-up planned.
problems: Varicose veins of unspecified lower extremity with inflammation

# GBS Septicemia:
Patient was found to have GBS in ___ BCx bottles drawn 
separately in the ED. No source could be identified, but the 
lesions on the lower extremitites from the patient's 
lipodermatosclerosis are the most likely cause. The patient was 
started on ceftriaxone, and received 2 days of vancomycin prior 
to ___ speciation. Once a pansensitive GBS was identified, the 
patient was switched to amoxicillin, with a plan to complete a 
14 day course of antibiotics for GBS bacteremia. A TTE was done 
that showed an EF>60% with no evidence of vegetations. The 
patient showed marked improvement over her hospital course with 
resolution of her symptoms. 

# Abdominal discomfort/N&V
Patient presented with non-specific epigastric pain and 
generalized abdominal discomfort. Given her significant cardiac 
history, ECG was done that did not show any acute changes, and 
troponin x2 was negative. The patient's nausea and pain resolved 
after she was started on ceftriaxone. It is likely that her 
abdominal discomfort was related to the underlying bacteremia.
